newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures stop eroding late, end mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures stop eroding late, end mixed.

text.p: U.S. debt futures stopped eroding late and closed pit trading barely mixed.
After wandering inside very tight ranges during the morning, futures drifted to the day's lows after the two-year Treasury note sale drew somewhat less demand than anticipated.
The Dutch bidding auction produced a high yield of 5.885 percent, above forecasts for 5.87 percent. The bid/cover stood at 2.21, while non-competitive bids totalled $1.321 billion.
"It was kind of a sloppy auction, not very well-received but not as bad as some people thought," said one T-bond futures floor broker of the note sale.
"It was pretty weak, sloppy," said another T-bond futures floor broker of the note sale.
"They (bonds) didn't like it and neither did we," added a Eurodollar floor broker.
More supply will enter the market later this week when Treasury auctions $12.5 billion in five-year notes Wednesday and conducts a year-bill sale Thursday.

But traders said a late bit of shortcovering limited the downside Tuesday and shaved the long end's losses as traders braced for Wednesday's first leg of Humphrey-Hawkins testimony by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.
Greenspan will complete the semi-annual ritual when he appears before a House committee March 5, which replaced the originally slated February 27 date.

Futures also dipped on talk, later confirmed, that weekly retail sales posted a strong gain. Adjusted retail sales rose 2.5 percent for the first three weeks of fiscal February versus January, according to Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook.

But other economic data Tuesday, including the 0.3-percent dip in BTM/Schroders weekly chain store sales and February consumer confidence that stood at 118.1 compared to forecasts for 116.1, had limited impact before Greenspan's testimony.
Fed vice chairman Alice Rivlin on Tuesday morning told a credit union group that the U.S. economy has produced as good a set of economic statistics in memory, perhaps ever.
Although some brokers said the verbiage made them slightly edgy about Wednesday's testimony, the market showed little measureable response to Rivlin's remarks.

The Fed's coupon pass at late-morning was largely expected and gave futures a fleeting boost to the session's peak as March T-bond futures probed above minor resistance at 112-27/32 to 112/29/32. It stalled below a more-important area at 113-01/32 to 113-03/32 before grinding back down.
The contract later nosed below support at about 112-21/32 after the tepid two-year auction but held above stronger levels pegged at the 112-13/32 area.

March T-bonds ended off 1/32 at 112-19/32, 10-year notes lost 1/32 to 109-16/32, munis rose 5/32 to 117-03/32, June T-bills ended off two bps at 94.92, and Eurodollars ended down two bps at 94.37. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
